title: 2017 AMC 10B 14
statement: An integer \(N\) is selected at random in the range \(1\leq N \leq 2020\) . What is the probability that the remainder when \(N^{16}\) is divided by \(5\) is \(1?\)

solutions.text:
By Fermat’s Little Theorem, \(N^4\equiv1\pmod5\) whenever \(N\) is not divisible by \(5.\) Therefore, \[N^{16}\equiv(N^4)^4\equiv1\pmod5.\]

There are \(\frac{2020}{5}=404\) multiples of \(5,\) so there are \(2020-404=1616\) allowable values of \(N.\)

A multiple of \(5\) has \(N^{16}\equiv0\pmod5,\) so no other values work. Thus the probability is \[\dfrac{1616}{2020}=\dfrac45.\]

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: Modulo \(5\), only whether \(N\) is divisible by \(5\) matters
Use Fermat’s little theorem or check residue classes modulo \(5\)
